A1.justification: Both PDFs describe BFS-Prover and retain corresponding method and experiment sections. All 11 pages of v1 and 12 pages of v3 are readable, including figures, equations, references, and v3's new proof appendix. v1 has no appendix.

before.justification: Section 3 reports original MiniF2F evaluations, SFT-versus-DPO scaling experiments, and proof-length and tactic-length distributions.

after.justification: Section 3 reports revised original MiniF2F evaluations and scaling results, alongside the retained distribution analyses.

M1.justification: Sections 2.1–2.3 retain the same LeanDojo integration, length-normalized priority score, beam-search filtering, cumulative SFT, and compiler-feedback DPO. The algorithmic steps and training objectives are unchanged; search-parameter revisions concern experimental settings.

E1.justification: Both versions use Mathlib, Lean-Github, Lean-Workbook, and autoformalized NuminaMath-CoT, with MiniF2F as the evaluation benchmark. The new IMO proof examples come from the existing MiniF2F test set and do not expand task coverage.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains DeepSeek-Prover-V1.5, InternLM2.5-StepProver, and HunyuanProver. Figure 4 retains the SFT-only versus SFT+DPO comparison. Newly cited provers are not added to the reported comparisons.

E3.justification: Settings change within the retained experimental design: expert-iteration sampling widths expand from 4/8 to 2/4/8, and fixed-budget evaluation changes alpha from 0.7 to 0.5. Accumulation replaces the alpha/temperature/width grid with alpha values {0.0, 0.5, 1.0}, holding other settings fixed. The scaling experiment reports 4096 total passes instead of 2048, while Table 1 retains its 2048 × 2 × 600 budget.

E4.justification: The new appendix adds five qualitative proof cases for IMO problems, illustrated in Figures 5–9. The existing proof/tactic distribution analyses and SFT-versus-DPO scaling study remain; no new component ablation or robustness test is introduced.

E5.justification: Table 1 newly reports 70.83% ± 0.89%, whereas v1 gives a single value. Both versions already describe sampling multiple pass@64 runs and show min–max ranges in Figure 4. v3 does not specify what the new ± statistic represents.

E6.justification: Table 1 replaces BFS-Prover's 68.85% fixed-budget and 71.31% accumulative results with 70.83% ± 0.89% and 72.95%. Figure 4 also changes: at 2048 passes, SFT/SFT+DPO move from 67.21%/68.85% to 70.38%/70.83%. These are revised results under changed search settings, not demonstrated same-setting gains. Comparator rankings remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The appendix newly supplies explicit mathematical statements and reported Lean proofs for five IMO problems in Figures 5–9. These are limited additions of benchmark proofs; the search-scoring formula and DPO mathematics remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract newly presents an openly released model as an output of the work. The three methodological contributions and the central claim that scaled BFS can achieve state-of-the-art MiniF2F performance without a critic or MCTS were already present in v1.

C2.justification: v3 removes the interpretation that DPO's advantage substantially widens with more search, retaining a claim of consistent benefit. Its expanded discussion and new Limitations section address diminishing returns from search, 7B model capacity, larger-model latency and memory tradeoffs, and long proof states exceeding practical context capacity.

D1.justification: v3 newly specifies Lean 4.7.0, discloses ten expert-iteration rounds for the evaluated checkpoint, and provides a model-release link. These disclosures do not establish a software-version or iteration-count change. Most training and infrastructure details remain, although Table 1 drops the explicit policy-model-size column.

R1.justification: The introduction adds references to BC-Prover, Lean-STaR, LEGO-Prover, TheoremLlama, autoformalization with LLMs, and the original DeepSeek-Prover. This broadens the cited context without substantially changing the positioning of BFS against MCTS and value-guided search.

P1.justification: The main section order and most methodological prose remain intact. Local edits refine terminology and experimental explanations; the conclusion gains discussion, and limitations and a proof appendix are added. The author-contribution and acknowledgement sections are removed.

P2.justification: The main document changes from one column to two columns, substantially altering text and float placement. Figures 2–4 are restyled or resized, Table 1 loses its policy-model-size column, and five boxed proof figures are added. Figure 1 retains its underlying diagram.

improvement.justification: v3 resolves v1's inconsistent headline scores and adds useful reproducibility disclosures, a reported model-release link, concrete proof examples, and substantive limitations. These improve clarity and inspectability. The gains remain limited: the table's uncertainty statistic is undefined, and changed search settings prevent treating the higher scores as a controlled performance improvement.
